LGTM ✅ — all four round-1 findings (F1–F4) are resolved and independently re-verified; the release-input delta introduces no new blocking issues.
Reviewed at 4b9ea56f0fd7466685ee57b196f6947c7de713a7 (round 2)

## Delta since db4c91f
- `4b9ea56` "Pin evaluator release build inputs" is the only functional commit: it pins all three `Dockerfile.evaluation` `FROM` stages to `@sha256:` digests and hash-pins the release build toolchain via a shared `packaging/evaluation/build-requirements.lock`.
- `aebf538` "Record council release input findings" is `.agentflow/` evidence only — non-reviewable generated artifacts.
- PR body was corrected: the four evaluator modules are now described as new (not pre-existing), and the artifact-hash/mtime claim is scoped as observed read-only replay behavior rather than a timestamp-restoration feature.
- Ancestry verified: `db4c91f` is reachable from head `4b9ea56` (linear, 2 new commits); scope confined to the packaging/release surface.

## Findings

| Resolved | Severity | Finding                                                                                                                                                      | Fixed in |
| -------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- |
| F1       | 🟡       | Docker build stages used mutable image tags — all three FROM lines now pin @sha256: digests                                                                  | 4b9ea56  |
| F2       | 🟡       | Release workflow installed an unpinned build backend — now installs from a hash-pinned build-requirements.lock via --require-hashes, shared by CI and Docker | 4b9ea56  |
| F3       | 🟡       | PR body mischaracterized the new evaluator modules as pre-existing — corrected to describe them as new                                                       | 4b9ea56  |
| F4       | 🟢       | PR body's hash/mtime "preserved" claim — corrected/scoped as observed read-only replay behavior                                                              | 4b9ea56  |

| F5  | 🟢       | Lock pins setuptools/pyproject-hooks/packaging/build but no explicit wheel; setuptools==84.0.0 vendors bdist_wheel so builds are expected to succeed, and the tag-triggered release workflow doesn't run on PR push — worth confirming on the first real evaluation-v* tag build. No action required in this PR. (raised by: rev-claude) | packaging/evaluation/build-requirements.lock:2 |

<details>
<summary>Finding Details</summary>

### 🟡 F1 (resolved): Docker base images pinned to digests
`Dockerfile.evaluation` now pins `python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:7824…2254` and both `node:22-bookworm-slim@sha256:83f4…a7e5` stages. Chair-verified at head; digests also match the recorded `base-image-digests.json` evidence per rev-claude.

### 🟡 F2 (resolved): Hash-pinned build toolchain
The release workflow installs the builder with `--require-hashes --requirement packaging/evaluation/build-requirements.lock` and builds with `--no-isolation`; the Dockerfile `package-build` stage uses the identical lock and `--no-build-isolation --no-deps`. The lock pins `setuptools==84.0.0`, `pyproject-hooks==1.2.0`, `packaging==26.3`, `build==1.6.0`, each with a `sha256` hash. CI and Docker genuinely share one pinned toolchain. Chair- and both-reviewer-verified. apt/npm registry resolution remains an explicit, documented non-goal (no bit-for-bit reproducibility claim).

### 🟡 F3 (resolved): PR body corrected
The description now states the four evaluator modules are new relative to `main`, including the security-sensitive OCI execution and artifact verification — removing the under-scrutiny risk flagged in round 1.

### 🟢 F4 (resolved): mtime claim scoped
The body now clarifies the hash/mtime observation is "observed replay/read-only behavior, not an os.utime or timestamp-restoration feature in the weekly-report module," matching the code.

### 🟢 F5 (new): No explicit `wheel` pin in the lock
rev-claude noted the lock omits an explicit `wheel` entry. Modern `setuptools` (≥70.1, here 84.0.0) vendors the wheel backend, so `python -m build`/`pip wheel` under `--no-isolation` is expected to work. The `evaluation-release.yml` workflow triggers only on `evaluation-v*` tags, so this PR carries no end-to-end CI proof of the build. Low confidence, non-blocking; confirm on the first tag build.

</details>

<details>
<summary>What's Good (🟢)</summary>

- SHA-bound review authority: `canonical_commit_id` rejects malformed/mismatched SHAs; `enforce_authority_write` fails closed on non-`verified` dispositions (from round 1, unregressed).
- Both round-1 security findings closed with immutable digests and a hash-verified, CI/Docker-shared build lock.
- Evaluator OCI executor and weekly report fail closed on hash/digest mismatch.
- Packaging runs nonroot end-to-end (uid 65532); launcher allowlists exactly three auth env vars and bind-mounts the repo read-only.
- Delta is tightly scoped to packaging/release inputs; no unrelated Rust/evaluator logic touched.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Baseline Check</summary>

- Re-review of round 1 (verdict at `db4c91f`, CHANGES REQUESTED). Prior SHA reachable from head; delta = 2 commits, 1 functional + 1 evidence-only.
- Net-new value this round: source-binding of the published image and Python artifacts, plus accurate PR-body claims.
- CI/checks: `rust` check in progress; combined status pending (0 contexts) at head. The tag-triggered release workflow does not run on PR push, so packaging/lock correctness is unverified by CI in this PR — consistent with round 1's noted limitation.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Review Metadata</summary>

- Reviewers: rev-codex (approve — security/source-binding, F1/F2 resolved, no new security issues), rev-claude (approve — correctness/integration, F1–F4 resolved, one non-blocking 🟢 candidate).
- Consensus: **approve**
- Absent reviewers: none

</details>
